newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Orogen looks at 10 pct Ok Tedi stake.
newsitem.headline: Orogen looks at 10 pct Ok Tedi stake.

text.p: Papua New Guinea resources group Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it had begun due diligence on acquiring a 10 percent stake in the Ok Tedi copper mine held by the PNG government.

Orogen was also considering purchasing an additional five percent stake in the Porgera gold project, and an extra two percent of the Kutubu oil project, managing director Charles Lepani told a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.
Lepani said the government was currently moving to transfer its interest in Porgera to the Mineral Resources Development Co Ltd, the first stage of acquisition by Orogen, he said.
"It's at very early stages at the moment," Orogen director Kevin McCann later told reporters.
"But by the end of the year we would want to in a position to know whether we wish to proceed or not," McCann said.
Lepani said the PNG government had endorsed a solution to environmental problems at Ok Tedi through the construction of a US$60 million tailings impoundment system over two years.
A solution to environmental problems was of key importance.
"We want to ensure that the environmental issues are clean enough not to get into problems if we take the interest," he said.
Orogen, which is 51 per cent owned by the Papua New Guinea government, has the right to acquire one third of the state's 30 percent stake in Ok Tedi at any time before January 1, 2000.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd has a 52.6 percent stake in Ok Tedi and Canada's Inmet Mining Corp 17.4 percent. Lepani said the extra five percent stake in the Placer Dome Inc -operated Porgera under consideration was a landowner option cancelled by the government.
The the additional two percent of the Chevron Corp -operated Kutubu oil project was held by the Gulf and Southern Highlands provincial governments.
Orogen already holds 15.0 percent of Porgera and 15.75 percent of Kutubu.
McCann said Orogen had a number of capital commitments and any decision on whether to take up the stakes had to be measured against other projects.
Lepani had held talks with Australian talks on a funding syndicate and the response had been "extremely good", McCann said.
